key_insight: Semantic Pareto-DQN reframes fraud detection as multi-objective reinforcement learning, using language-model-based semantic states and Pareto-optimal rewards to avoid zero-recall collapse on rare anomalies.
engineering_relevance: The framework suggests a practical alternative to resampling and single-threshold classifiers for imbalanced financial monitoring, letting teams trade off fraud capture against customer friction explicitly.
method: Convert heterogeneous transaction features into natural-language narratives.
Encode narratives with large language models to build scale-invariant state representations.
Optimize a vector reward over financial efficacy, operational friction, and semantic discovery via Pareto-DQN.
evidence_signal: Across E-Commerce fraud and UCI Credit datasets, the method reports stronger minority-class recall than scalarized baselines and breaks the zero-recall trap.
watch_item: Performance may depend on high-quality narrative construction and careful reward design, and added LLM/DRL complexity could raise latency and deployment costs.
paper_title: Semantic Pareto-DQN: A Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Framework for Financial Anomaly Detection
